title: Resident Evil 2 Was 70% Finished When Capcom Scrapped It
hook: Capcom had Resident Evil 2 about 70 percent done in 1997, with a motorcycle racer named Elza Walker instead of Claire. Shinji Mikami played it, called it no fun, and the whole thing was rebuilt from scratch. Would you have shipped the first version?
sources: https://gematsu.com/2026/05/capcom-platinum-titles-sales-update-as-of-march-31-2026 (Capcom Platinum Titles: RE2 4.96 million, RE1 2.75 million)
https://xbox.com/en-GB/games/store/1/BZ271JBBZ9DC (RE2 Deluxe Edition listing: Elza Walker costume)
script: Did you know Resident Evil Two was about seventy percent finished when Capcom threw it away and started over? The original Resident Evil launched in March of nineteen ninety six and sold millions of copies. Capcom began the sequel almost right away, with a rookie director named Hideki Kamiya in charge. The game was aimed at a May nineteen ninety seven release. Leon Kennedy was already in it, but his partner was not Claire Redfield. She was Elza Walker, a college student and motorcycle racer who crashed her bike straight into the Raccoon City police station. Then producer Shinji Mikami played through the build and decided it simply was not fun. He later said no single part was boring, just everything as a whole. So a game that was roughly two thirds done was scrapped, and the team rebuilt it from scratch. Elza became Claire, the story was rewritten, and Resident Evil Two finally shipped in January of nineteen ninety eight. It went on to sell almost five million copies on the original PlayStation. The abandoned version is now known as Resident Evil One Point Five, and a leaked build still floats around online. Capcom even gave Claire an Elza Walker costume in the remake. Would you have shipped the first version? Follow for more gaming history.
